text.p: Roman Catholic Cardinal Jean Jerome Hamer of Belgium has died at the age of 80, the Vatican said on Monday.
Hamer, who was born in Brussels on June 1, 1916, had served as prefect of the Vatican's Congregation for Institutes of Consecrated Life and Societies of Apostolic Life.
The Vatican said Hamer, elevated to cardinal by Pope John Paul in May 1985, died at the Gemelli Hospital in Rome. It did not give the cause of death.

The Pope sent a telegram of condolence to Cardinal Bernardin Gantin, deacon of the College of Cardinals, in which he praised Hamer for his "theological preparation and his testimony of faith to the church", the Vatican said.
Hamer participated as a theological expert during the debate about the direction of the Catholic Church that raged during the Second Vatican Council of 1962 to 1965.
